models.name: Claude Fable 5.2
models.notes: Anthropic's current Fable-tier model: 'For demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work'. Released November 9, 2026 ('Latest. Released November 9, 2026' on its model page; Status 'Active (latest)'); the deprecations table reads Active with a tentative retirement not sooner than November 9, 2027. $8 in / $40 out per MTok. 5m cache write $10/MTok, 1h cache write $16/MTok; the cached_input field carries the cache-read rate, which on this model is 2.5% of input ($0.20/MTok) instead of the usual 10%. Batch $4 in / $20 out. Fast mode (Messages API, no beta header) $16 in / $80 out. Adaptive thinking always on (cannot be turned off); effort defaults to high. 1M context, 128K max output. Reliable knowledge cutoff Jun 2026; training data cutoff Jun 2026. Requires 30-day data retention (not available under zero data retention unless expressly authorized by Anthropic). Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed and Google managed) and Microsoft Foundry; the same model is offered to verified organizations as Claude Mythos 5.2. Supersedes Claude Fable 5.1, now a legacy model. Added 2026-11-16, a week after release: the delay is ours.

models.name: GPT-6.2 Astra
models.notes: Released 2026-11-17 per OpenAI's own API changelog ("Use GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding reasoning and coding tasks"); the model page calls it "Our most capable model for your hardest projects". May 18 2026 knowledge cutoff. Text+image input, text output (audio and video unsupported); 1,050,000-token context (maximum input 922,000), 128,000 max output. Reasoning tokens supported; the API rejects reasoning effort 'none'. Tool calling requires the Responses API; Chat Completions is supported. Standard tier per 1M as stated on the model page and in the pricing page's Standard table: $8.00 in / $0.40 cached in / $10.00 cache write / $40.00 out. The cache write rate is for 30-minute retention; a 12-hour cache write is priced separately on the model page. For requests with more than 272K input tokens, input and cache rates double and output is 1.5x for the full request; the price fields carry the <=272K band. Batch is 50% of Standard and Fast mode is 2x Standard. Ultrafast is a dated SCHEDULE, not one multiplier: 3x Standard through 2027-02-28 and 6x Standard from 2027-03-01 (Pacific time) - no price field here carries Ultrafast, so the cutover does not move any field. Discounted background completion windows (Responses API public beta, announced 2026-11-17) bill token rates 30% below Standard for the 2-hour window and 40% below for the 8-hour window. Snapshot list on the model page is the bare alias only; no dated snapshot is published. STATUS: recorded as ga on the same reading as GPT-6.1 Sol - the changelog entry is tagged Feature with v1/responses and v1/chat/completions, the model page carries no access or rollout qualifier, and OpenAI does not use the words "generally available". Lifecycle fields are null: OpenAI announces no deprecation alongside this release and its deprecations page names neither GPT-6.2 model. Found 2026-11-18 by check-pricing-prose (new GPT-6.2 lines on the pricing page) and check-price-drift ("priced by OpenAI, not in our catalog" 11 -> 13); the one-day delay is ours. Every Standard rate is below GPT-6 Astra's (see that row); OpenAI does not deprecate GPT-6 Astra with this release.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.notes: OpenAI's new top model, released 2026-09-03 per its own API changelog ("Released GPT-6 Astra, our most capable model, built for the hardest end-to-end work", tagged v1/responses and v1/chat/completions). Text+image input, text output; 1,050,000-token context, 128,000 max output, Apr 30 2026 knowledge cutoff. reasoning.effort supports low/medium/high/xhigh/max - the 'none' level is NOT supported, and neither are custom temperature/top_p or logprobs; tool calling requires the Responses API. Standard tier per 1M: $10.00 in / $1.00 cached in / $12.50 cache write / $50.00 out. Batch and Flex are 50% of Standard ($5.00/$0.50/$6.25/$25.00); Fast mode is 2x ($20.00/$2.00/$25.00/$100.00) and is unavailable with EU data residency. models.name: Gemini Decision
models.notes: A specialized decision/classification model for Google's new Decisions API (client.decisions.create, REST POST /v1beta/decisions), not a text generator: per the model page it 'evaluates typed questions over text, images, video, audio, and PDFs in a single prefill pass and returns calibrated outcome probabilities with zero output tokens' - yes/no (probability 0.01-0.99 plus confidence), single-select over 2-255 options, and rubric rating over 2-255 ordered levels, up to 1,000 independent questions per request over shared input. STATUS SIGNAL, stated so a consumer can weigh it: Google labels this model neither 'Stable'/'GA' nor 'Preview' anywhere we read. status 'ga' rests on Google's own naming convention on the models page ('Model version name patterns', convention as of September 2025: preview model strings carry a -preview suffix, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025, while a plain string 'points to a specific stable model'); gemini-decision-1 has no suffix, the model page's Versions field lists only that string, the November 11, 2026 release note says 'Released' with no preview qualifier, and the deprecations page lists it in its own 'Gemini Decision models' table rather than under a preview heading. Note the SDK examples call api_version v1beta. Pricing (paid tier, per 1M tokens): input /usr/bin/bash.10 for text, image, video, audio and PDF alike; output 'Not applicable (0 output tokens)', so price_output_per_mtok is null; context caching 'Not available'; Batch API not supported; free tier input is free of charge. Google bills shared input tokens once per request regardless of question count, and each question adds tokens for its own instructions, criteria and formatting. Token limits from the model page: input 262,144 (context_window); output token limit published as 0 ('up to 1,000 questions per request') - max_output_tokens is left null, following the convention of the catalog's embedding and rerank rows, because the model generates no tokens. Released 2026-11-11 per the API release notes and the deprecations table ('No shutdown date announced', no replacement); the model page's 'Latest update' reads 'November 2026'. No knowledge cutoff is published, so that stays null. First read 2026-11-12, one day after Google's date.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image 2.0

This is the declared redirect target for grok-imagine-image-quality from 2026-11-02, serving that slug at quality 'low'. released is null as a SOURCED ABSENCE: xAI's release notes carry no launch entry naming this slug - it first appears already in service in the 2026-08-28 entry - so no launch date is dated anywhere first-party and none is invented here.

models.name: Grok Imagine Image (Quality)

So the slug STILL RESOLVES, but the model behind it is gone: callers get grok-imagine-image-2.0 at 'low' quality and a lower price, and gRPC responses report grok-imagine-image-2.0-low as the model. From 2026-09-18 to 2026-11-04 the row was held at deprecated on xAI's 60-day notice (opened 2026-09-02); before 2026-09-18 it wrongly published 'ga' with no lifecycle dates, 16 days after the announcement. The retired grok-imagine-image-pro (2026-05-15) redirected here and is now likewise served by grok-imagine-image-2.0-low. Standard tier grok-imagine-image (1.0) is not affected.

models.name: Grok TTS
models.notes: Text-to-speech model, and the only row in this catalog billed per character, so the token price fields are null by design. xAI publishes the rate on its pricing page as $15.00 / 1M chars under 'Voice API', i.e. $0.000015 per character, and the models-index hydration payload carries the same figure as an integer in the 1e-10 USD units this catalog calibrated against two rows it already held: 'pricing': {'perCharacter': '150000'}. Input is text, output is audio - there is no token accounting on either side, so a caller budgets by character count, not by tokens. Request limits, from the reference: maximum 60,000 characters of text per request; voice_id defaults to 'eve'; a BCP-47 language code is required and 'auto' enables detection; output defaults to MP3 at 24 kHz / 128 kbps, with telephony-optimised mu-law among the other formats; speech tags control delivery inline. Custom voices cloned from a short clip can be used here and with the Speech to Speech API. Rate limits at the base tier are 50 rps / 3,000 rpm / 100 concurrent sessions, rising to 1,000 rps / 60,000 rpm at tier 5. RELEASED IS NULL AS A SOURCED ABSENCE, NOT A MISSING FIELD: xAI's release notes date the Text-to-Speech API going generally available to 2026-03-16 ('The Text-to-Speech API is now generally available'), but that entry does not name this model slug, and no release-notes entry anywhere on the page does - so the API has a first-party date and the model does not. Added to the catalog 2026-09-19 as a completeness fix; xAI published nothing on this date.

models.name: Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0
models.notes: Speech-to-text model, billed by duration of audio rather than by token, so the token price fields are null by design. TWO RATES, NOT ONE, AND THE MODE DECIDES WHICH: xAI's pricing page lists Speech to Text at $0.10 per hour (REST) and $0.20 per hour (Streaming) - streaming is exactly double - and the models-index hydration payload carries both as integers in the 1e-10 USD-per-second units this catalog calibrated against rows it already held: 'perAudioSecond': '277778' and 'perAudioSecondStreaming': '555556'. Released 2026-09-17, dated by xAI's own release notes: 'grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 is now available. Use grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 or grok-voice-transcribe-2.0'. THE DEFAULT MODEL IS CONTRADICTED ACROSS TWO FIRST-PARTY SURFACES and this catalog does not pick a winner: that release-notes entry says 'the default is grok-voice-transcribe-1.0', while the Speech to Text reference prints grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 in the model parameter's default cell. Set model explicitly and the question does not arise. Capabilities, from the reference: 25 languages, batch and streaming modes, 12 audio formats, word-level timestamps, multichannel transcription (2-8 channels), speaker diarization, Smart Turn end-of-turn detection, and a vad_threshold parameter that tunes the voice-activity gate (0 disables it). Maximum 500 MB per file, or a URL the server downloads. Rate limits at the base tier are 10 rps / 600 rpm / 100 concurrent sessions. Added to the catalog 2026-09-19, two days after release.

models.name: Grok Voice Transcribe 1.0

Billed by duration of audio, not by token, so the token price fields are null by design. SAME RATE AS 2.0 ON BOTH AXES, and that is first-party twice over: xAI's pricing page publishes one Speech to Text line for the mode rather than one per model ($0.10 per hour REST, $0.20 per hour streaming), and the models-index hydration payload carries byte-identical integers for the two models ('perAudioSecond': '277778', 'perAudioSecondStreaming': '555556') in the 1e-10 USD-per-second units this catalog calibrated against rows it already held. Rate limits at the base tier are also identical: 10 rps / 600 rpm / 100 concurrent sessions. RELEASED IS NULL AS A SOURCED ABSENCE: xAI's release notes date the Speech to Text API going generally available to 2026-04-15 ('The xAI Speech to Text API is now generally available. Transcribe audio to text in 25 languages with batch and streaming modes'), but that entry does not name this model slug and no entry on the page does, so the API has a first-party date and the model does not. Added to the catalog 2026-09-19 as a completeness fix; xAI published nothing on this date.

models.name: Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0
models.notes: Realtime speech-to-speech model for voice agents, driven over a WebSocket at wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime with low-latency turn-taking and server-side tool use. Billed by connected audio time and by session concurrency rather than by token, so the token price fields are null by design. Released 2026-07-29, dated by xAI's own release notes ('grok-voice-think-fast-2.0 is now available with Speech to Speech'), and the alias grok-voice-latest was stated in the same entry to route here from 2026-08-05 - so an application pinned to that alias moved to this model on that date without changing a string. THE PUBLISHED RATE IS $0.08 per minute of audio, which xAI itself also prints as $4.80/hr, and the models-index hydration payload agrees: 'realtimeAudioSecondPrice': '13333333' in the 1e-10 USD units this catalog calibrated against rows it already held, which is $0.0013333 per second. The payload additionally carries 'pstnMinutePrice': '100000000' - $0.01 per minute, the same integer this catalog already publishes as $0.01 per image elsewhere in xAI's payload, so the unit is confirmed rather than assumed - for sessions bridged to the public telephone network. TWO FURTHER PAYLOAD FIELDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED, and this is a closed path rather than an oversight: 'realtimeAudioTokenPrice': '266667' and 'realtimeTextInputPrice': '40000000' cannot both be read in the per-token unit that works everywhere else in this payload - the second would come out four orders of magnitude above any published rate - and xAI's pricing page prints the second one as a bare figure of $0.004 for realtime text with no denominator at all, so neither surface establishes what either field is per. A figure whose unit is unknown is not a price, and this catalog will not publish one. Session concurrency is the rate-limit axis: 10 concurrent sessions at the base tier, 20 / 50 / 100 / 200 / 400 at tiers 1 to 5. A first-generation grok-voice-think-fast-1.0 was released 2026-04-23 and is absent from the current models payload; this catalog does NOT infer a retirement from that absence and carries no row for it. Added to the catalog 2026-09-19 as a completeness fix; xAI published nothing on this date.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
models.notes: DeepSeek's first model on its new architecture family, released 2026-09-10 and dated first-hand by DeepSeek's own Change Log entry for that day: 'Today, we officially release the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model. It is the smallest model in our new architecture family, with native multimodal visual understanding.' Call it as deepseek-flash — that is the model name DeepSeek instructs you to use, and it is why api_string is not the row id. PRICES ARE A PEAK / OFF-PEAK PAIR, so read the column, not the number: the fields above carry the PEAK rates per 1M tokens ($0.30 cache-miss input, $1.20 output, $0.006 cache-hit input), and off-peak is exactly half on every axis ($0.15 / $0.60 / $0.003). DeepSeek states, as revised on or just before 2026-09-19, 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full.' - so off-peak is what you pay for most of the week, and on a Chinese public holiday you pay it around the clock. Until that revision the same footnote read 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday (all other hours are off-peak)', with no holiday carve-out; this catalog's prose baseline carried the old wording on 2026-09-18 and the new wording on 2026-09-19, and DeepSeek dated the edit nowhere. No rate moved. The fields track peak because DeepSeek presents peak as the rate and off-peak as half of it, which is the same convention this catalog has applied to the V4 rows since the 2026-08-16 cutover. That makes this a genuine price cut for the Flash line, and DeepSeek says so in the same Change Log entry ('With the release of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, API prices have been reduced accordingly'): the model it replaces, deepseek-v4-flash, was $0.44 / $1.32 / $0.014 at peak, so input falls ~32%, output ~9% and cache-hit input ~57%. Native vision: the feature table marks Vision supported for this model and 'Not supported' for deepseek-v4-pro, and the HuggingFace repo is tagged image-text-to-text, hence modality text + image. Thinking and non-thinking modes (thinking is the default), JSON output, tool calls, Responses API, Anthropic-format API and chat prefix completion all supported; FIM completion is non-thinking-mode only. Context length 1M, max output 384K, concurrency limit 2500. Open weights published the same day at huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under the MIT license (fp8/8-bit safetensors). Status is ga because DeepSeek announces it as an official release with no preview or experimental label — unlike the V4 generation, which it shipped as 'DeepSeek V4 Preview' and which this catalog therefore carried as preview. Knowledge cutoff is NOT published by DeepSeek, so the field is null rather than guessed. It is the stated destination for two retired endpoints: deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp both route here, their names still accepted but the models behind them retired. Until 2026-09-12 this note named a third, deepseek-v4-pro, as joining them at 12:00 Beijing Time on 2026-09-14; DeepSeek has since withdrawn that retirement - 'we have decided to continue providing API services for DeepSeek V4 Pro after September 14, 2026, with the billing method remaining unchanged' - so V4 Pro stays live on its own rates and does not route here. MODEL VERSION: since 2026-10-17 deepseek-flash serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an in-place upgrade under the same name; DeepSeek's Change Log entry for that day reads 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has been upgraded to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 ... The API calling method and pricing remain unchanged', and the Models & Pricing page's MODEL VERSION row now reads DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. No field of this row changed with it: same id, same api_string, same rates, same 1M context and 384K max output. Until 2026-10-17 the name served the original DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash release of 2026-09-10. The pricing page is served at the TRAILING-SLASH url; the extensionless form returns a different document ('Your First API Call') with HTTP 200.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
models.notes: Experimental multimodal vision-understanding sibling of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and one of the shortest-lived endpoints in this catalog: released 2026-08-21 and retired 2026-09-10, twenty days later. Both dates are DeepSeek's own, from its Change Log — 'Today, the new multimodal vision understanding model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp is now available on the DeepSeek API platform. This is an experimental model that can be accessed by setting model=deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp' (2026-08-21), and 'The previous-generation models V4 Flash and V4 Flash Vision Exp have been retired; for compatibility, the model names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are temporarily routed to V4.1 Flash' (2026-09-10). RETIREMENT SIGNAL: an explicit past-tense statement by the provider, on a dated announcement — not an inference from the model disappearing off the pricing page, though it did also disappear from it the same day. The name is still ACCEPTED by the API, so calls do not fail; they are served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and billed at the Flash price, and DeepSeek calls that routing 'temporary'. On DeepSeek's own benchmarks it was on par with V4-Flash on pure text and a significant step up on visual agent tasks. PRICES ABOVE ARE THE RATES IN FORCE AT RETIREMENT and deliberately stop tracking anything: PEAK per 1M was $0.014 cache-hit / $0.44 cache-miss / $1.32 out, off-peak exactly half ($0.007 / $0.22 / $0.66), identical to deepseek-v4-flash on every axis, with images converted to input tokens by dimension. Those figures come from DeepSeek's pricing page as it stood on 2026-09-07, read from the Internet Archive snapshot cited below, because the live page dropped the column on the day of retirement — this row was added on 2026-09-10, after the fact, so the archived first-party document is the only surface that still carries them. Context 1M, max output 384K, concurrency limit 2500, JSON output / tool calls / Responses API / Anthropic API / chat prefix completion supported, FIM completion NOT supported (it was the only V4 endpoint where FIM was unavailable). Knowledge cutoff never published. Open weights at huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp.

Signal: an explicit past-tense statement by the provider on a dated announcement — DeepSeek's Change Log entry for 2026-09-10 reads 'The previous-generation models V4 Flash and V4 Flash Vision Exp have been retired; for compatibility, the model names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are temporarily routed to V4.1 Flash', and the pricing page footnote said the same until 2026-10-17: 'The legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired, their requests are served by the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model and billed at the Flash price.' Since 2026-10-17 it reads 'served by the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model', DeepSeek's in-place upgrade of deepseek-flash that day; the retirement wording is unchanged. That is a statement, not an inference from the column vanishing off the pricing page, though it vanished the same day. DeepSeek published no separate shutdown date and no deprecation window: one date, so this row carries it in retires_on only and leaves deprecated_on null. THE NAME STILL WORKS — calls do not fail, they are served by V4.1-Flash and billed at the cheaper Flash price, and DeepSeek calls that routing 'temporary', so consumers should migrate to deepseek-flash rather than rely on it. Until 2026-09-10 this row was carried as preview, on the grounds that it was part of the 'DeepSeek V4 Preview' generation released 2026-04-24, and that was right for the period it covered. PRICES ABOVE ARE THE RATES IN FORCE AT RETIREMENT and deliberately no longer track the endpoint that now serves the traffic: PEAK $0.014/M cache-hit, $0.44/M cache-miss, $1.32/M out, with off-peak exactly half. V4.1-Flash is cheaper on every axis ($0.006 / $0.30 / $1.20 peak), so a caller left on the legacy name is billed at the new, lower Flash price, not at these. Historical spec, unchanged: smaller/cheaper V4 model (~284B total / ~13B active params per authoritative third-party reports), 1M context, 384K max output, dual Thinking / Non-Thinking modes, JSON output, tool calls, chat prefix completion, FIM completion in non-thinking mode only, Responses API and Anthropic-format API supported, concurrency limit 2500, open weights. The legacy aliases deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner pointed here and were themselves retired 2026-07-24, which makes that pair a two-hop chain to deepseek-v4-1-flash; each row records the target its provider named at the time rather than being silently re-pointed. Prior lifecycle of this row, kept because it explains the price fields: DeepSeek moved API billing to peak/off-peak at 16:00 UTC on 2026-08-16, having announced it undated on 2026-08-13 and dated on 2026-08-14; the fields were re-pointed at the PEAK column on the cutover day, about 8 hours early, because this catalog refreshes once daily at ~08:05 UTC and the alternative was publishing superseded rates for ~16 hours. That window closed on 2026-08-17.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.notes: GA on DeepSeek's own declaration, in its API Change Log for 2026-08-13: 'The GA release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro has been rolled out on the APP, Web, and API. The API calling method remains unchanged - simply set the model name to deepseek-v4-pro to use the latest version.' DEPRECATION WITHDRAWN BY THE PROVIDER. Until 2026-09-12 this row was held at deprecated, with deprecated_on 2026-09-10 and retires_on 2026-09-14, on DeepSeek's announcement that it would retire V4 Pro at 12:00 Beijing Time on 2026-09-14 and route the name to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at the Flash price; that announcement has been reversed and no longer exists on either surface that carried it. DeepSeek states: 'In response to user demand, we have decided to continue providing API services for DeepSeek V4 Pro after September 14, 2026, with the billing method remaining unchanged. We will provide further notice should there be any changes.' THE SIGNAL IS THAT STATEMENT, read first-hand from the raw HTML of api-docs.deepseek.com - not an inference from the model still appearing in the rate table. Where it lives changed on 2026-09-19: from 2026-09-12 until then it was carried BOTH as footnote (2) beside the live rate column on the Models & Pricing page and as a paragraph in the Change Log entry for 2026-09-10; the pricing-page footnote has since been removed - September 14 is past, and footnote (2) on that page is now the peak/off-peak schedule - while the Change Log paragraph is still there, re-read first-hand today. The withdrawal therefore still stands on one first-party surface, not two, and V4 Pro is still listed with live rates in the rate table. deprecated_on, retires_on and replacement are therefore null again, because the provider now states no deprecation, no shutdown date and no successor; the 'we will provide further notice should there be any changes' clause is DeepSeek's own and is why this is a withdrawal rather than a guarantee. DeepSeek gives NO DATE for the reversal itself - it edited its 2026-09-10 Change Log entry in place rather than adding a new one - so the only bound on when it published is this catalog's prose baseline, which held the retirement text on 2026-09-11 and the withdrawal text on 2026-09-12. Separately, and as a correction rather than a provider event: this row was carried as preview until 2026-09-10 on our own inference that it belonged to the 'DeepSeek V4 Preview' generation released 2026-04-24, while DeepSeek had in fact declared GA on 2026-08-13 and this catalog did not act on it. The deprecation made that moot for two days; the withdrawal makes it live again, so the row returns to the status the provider declares rather than to the one we had inferred. PRICES ARE UNCHANGED and DeepSeek states the billing method is unchanged: PEAK per 1M is $0.044 cache-hit / $1.32 cache-miss / $3.96 out, with OFF-PEAK exactly half ($0.022 / $0.66 / $1.98). The fields carry the PEAK column by the convention this catalog adopted at the 2026-08-16 peak/off-peak cutover, because DeepSeek presents peak as the rate and off-peak as half of it. The peak window is narrow and got narrower on or just before 2026-09-19: 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full.' Off-peak therefore covers every weekend hour, every Chinese public holiday in full, and most weekday hours. Until that revision the footnote read 'Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday (all other hours are off-peak)', with no holiday carve-out, and no rate moved with the change. Spec, unchanged: largest V4 model (~1.6T total / ~49B active params per its HuggingFace model card and authoritative third-party reports; MIT licence; mixed FP4/FP8), 1M context, 384K max output, three reasoning-effort modes (non-think / think high / think max), JSON output, tool calls, Responses API and Anthropic-format API supported, chat prefix completion, FIM completion in non-thinking mode only, concurrency limit 500, VISION NOT SUPPORTED (the feature table marks it 'Not supported' here and supported on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Model version string: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813. Knowledge cutoff never published by DeepSeek, so it stays null. The pricing page is served at the TRAILING-SLASH url (2026-08-11): the extensionless form returns a different document ("Your First API Call") with HTTP 200.

models.name: Amazon Nova Premier
models.notes: Most capable Nova 1 model: complex reasoning, agentic workflows, model distillation. Reasoning supported. 1M-token context, 25K max output. Model card states lifecycle = 'Legacy' and 'Model EOL date: September 14, 2026'; the row is held at 'deprecated' (= Legacy), which is what AWS declares. Until 2026-09-15 this note read that EOL date as a firm retirement — that reading did not survive the date. Re-read first-hand on 2026-09-15, the day AFTER the stated EOL: the card still said 'Model lifecycle: Legacy' and still carried the same EOL date, so the status stayed 'deprecated'; the signal used then was the card's own lifecycle field, and a shutdown date that has merely passed is not a retirement signal on its own. The same card also stated 'EOL no sooner than: Oct 31, 2026' beside 'Model EOL date: September 14, 2026' — two first-party fields that contradicted each other; both are recorded verbatim here and neither is resolved into our typed fields. OBSERVED 2026-10-06: the Bedrock model card URL (bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-amazon-nova-premier.html, this row's source_url until today) now 302-redirects to the Bedrock user-guide root, and Nova Premier is absent from Bedrock's 'Models at a glance' page while Nova Pro, Lite, Micro and 2 Lite are listed there and their cards still resolve. The Nova user guide (what-is-nova.html, now this row's source_url) still lists Nova Premier as an understanding model with model ID amazon.nova-premier-v1:0 and inference profile us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0, and the us-east-1 Price List book published 2026-10-05T21:04Z still carries 28 Nova Premier SKUs at exactly the rates this row holds. The lifecycle statements ('Legacy', the EOL dates) are no longer published anywhere we can find: a deleted page is an absence, not a declaration, so the status stays 'deprecated' and the signal used today is 'still priced in the current book + still listed by the Nova guide', not the vanished card. NOTE: model card shows 'Model launch date: Oct 31, 2025' which conflicts with the public GA of Nova Premier (Apr/May 2025); the Oct 31 2025 date may reflect a card/version update rather than original GA — flagged as uncertain. Only us. geo inference ID (us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0). The Price List API (us-east-1, 2026-09-11 book) publishes the rates per 1K tokens as $0.0025/1K input, $0.0125/1K output and $0.000625/1K cache read, which is exactly the $2.50 / $12.50 / $0.625 per 1M this row carries. That last sentence had been cut mid-word, immediately after the first per-1K figure, since the repo's initial import, which truncated this note at exactly 600 characters; the tail is restored from the Price List API, not reconstructed.

Billed PER SEARCH UNIT, not per token — AWS defines a search unit as one query containing up to 100 document chunks (docs: 'Reranking is priced per query. Rate is the us-west-2 on-demand price from the AWS Price List API (SKU Z7M6S4MRBXNXJRB4: $0.001 per search unit = $1.00 per 1,000). Text only. Single-region model: ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, us-west-2 — explicitly NOT available in us-east-1, where Cohere Rerank 3.5 is the only reranker. No token context window is published (the limit is expressed in document chunks per query), and AWS declares no deprecation or EOL date, so those fields stay null. No release date published in the docs, so `released` is null rather than invented.

Supports image uploads (added Apr 2025) and file attachments PDF/DOC/DOCX/TXT/RTF (added Sep 2025). Max output tokens not published by Perplexity. Knowledge cutoff not published (search-grounded model with live web access). Pricing page fetched 2026-06-28; token and request rates re-read unchanged on the pricing page 2026-09-29, which still publishes the Sonar API tables. LIFECYCLE (read 2026-09-29): Perplexity's Sonar migration guide states 'Sonar Chat Completions support ended on September 27, 2026. Synchronous and streaming requests keep working: they are being reformulated as Agent API requests, rolling out gradually by model. Asynchronous Sonar requests are not reformulated and are no longer supported'. The changelog files the migration under 'Deprecation' (July 2026, no day given), so deprecated_on carries the stated support-end date, 2026-09-27. Signal used: that first-party sentence. Status is deprecated, NOT retired: Perplexity says synchronous calls still work and states no shutdown date, so retires_on stays null. Perplexity's comparable Agent API preset for Sonar is 'fast' (migration guide mapping table); presets are not catalog models, so replacement stays null. The former per-model docs page now redirects to the migration guide.

models.name: Gemini Nano Banana 2.1
models.notes: Image generation and conversational editing; Google's release note (2026-10-06) calls it "An update to Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image)" and announces it generally available, with wide and panoramic aspect ratios (1:4, 4:1, 1:8, 8:1) across 1K, 2K and 4K. Input $1.50/1M labelled text/image/video. Two output rates: text and thinking tokens $7.50/1M, image tokens $30.00/1M - price_output_per_mtok holds the image rate (the model's product). Google states the per-image equivalents: $0.0336 per 1K image (1024x1024px, 1120 tokens), $0.0504 per 2K (1680 tokens), $0.113 per 4K (3780 tokens). Batch tier $0.75 in / $3.75 text out / $15.00 image out. Paid tier only (free tier "Not available"). Grounding with Google Web and Image Search: 5,000 free requests per month shared across all Gemini 3.x models, then $14 per 1,000 requests. Released October 6, 2026 per Google's release notes and the Release date column of the deprecations table ("No shutdown date announced"). Google names it the recommended replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-image (deprecated the same day), the greyed gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview, gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview and gemini-2.0-flash-preview-image-generation, and the three Imagen 4 models. No context window or max output published for this model.

models.name: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
models.notes: Video generation and editing; successor to gemini-omni-1.1-flash, which Google auto-routes here from December 3, 2026. Google's changelog entry of November 5, 2026 announces it generally available, with up to 15-second video generation and conversational editing (3-10s for first and last frame interpolation, 3-10s per-turn video extension up to 30s total), better character and subject consistency across up to 6 reference images, 30% lower video output pricing and doubled paid-tier rate limits. The model page Versions block reads 'Stable: gemini-omni-1.2-flash'; the deprecations table gives release date November 5, 2026 and 'No shutdown date announced'. Paid tier only: the pricing page states 'Not available' on the free tier. Input $1.50 per 1M (labelled text / image / video). Two output rates (including thinking tokens): text $9.00/1M, video $12.00/1M — price_output_per_mtok holds the video rate, the same convention as gemini-omni-1.1-flash. Google bills on total output tokens at 5,792 tokens per second of 720p video, an effective ~$0.07/s (~$0.70 for a 10s clip); it also quotes $0.023/s at 360p (1,931 tokens/s), $0.104/s at 1080p with upsampling (8,688 tokens/s) and $0.209/s at 4K with upsampling (17,376 tokens/s). Limits per the model page: input 131,072 tokens, output 65,536 tokens, output video 3s-15s at 360p/720p/1080p/4K, 24 FPS. Model page lists inputs Text, Image, Video. No context caching rate is published. Read first-party 2026-11-07 from aistudio.google.com/docs (pricing, model page, deprecations, changelog).

models.name: Genie 4
models.notes: Real-time interactive world generation on the Interactions API (v1beta): seed a world from a text prompt, a 16:9 reference image, or both, then steer the live 24 fps 16:9 video with synchronized 48 kHz stereo audio using keyboard controls (WASD/arrow keys) and mid-session text events, streamed over WebRTC or WebSockets. Google's changelog entry of November 19, 2026 is headed 'Genie 4 (genie-4) generally available (GA)'; the model page Versions block reads 'Stable: genie-4' and its 'Latest update' field says 'November 2026'; the deprecations page 'Genie models' table gives release date November 19, 2026, 'No shutdown date announced' and no replacement. Paid tier only (every free-tier cell reads 'Not available'). Single-column pricing with no dated schedule: input $1.50 per 1M (text / reference image); two output rates - text $9.00/1M and video $17.50/1M (audio included) - price_output_per_mtok holds the VIDEO rate, the same convention as gemini-omni-1-2-flash. Google bills emitted video output tokens at 240 tokens per frame (5,760 tokens per second at 24 fps), which it states is an effective ~$0.10 per second (~$6.05 per minute). No context caching price; Batch API, Flex and Priority inference are not supported. Session limits per the model page: output video 1280x720 (720p), up to 120 seconds per session, a single 16:9 reference image; serving regions United States, Western Europe and Japan. Google publishes no context-window or output-token limit and no knowledge cutoff, so context_window, max_output_tokens and knowledge_cutoff stay null. For offline fixed-duration clips Google points to gemini-omni-1-2-flash instead (guidance, not a replacement). Read first-party 2026-11-20 from aistudio.google.com/docs (changelog, model page, pricing, deprecations).

models.notes: Speech-to-text. Audio in, text plus word annotations out, with automatic detection of 85+ languages, mid-session code-switching, speaker diarization (up to 8 speakers), word-level timestamps, smart dictation and formatting, and custom vocabulary biasing of up to 1,000 terms. Status ga because Google's models index badges the Gemini 3.5 Transcribe card 'New Stable' — one card covering both endpoints, gemini-3.5-transcribe and gemini-3.5-transcribe-live — and the id carries no -preview suffix; read 2026-09-01. Paid-tier rates per 1M tokens: input $2.00 on audio, output $12.00 on text. Google also publishes duration-equivalent figures for the same rates (roughly $0.003 per minute of audio in and $0.002 per minute of text out, on an assumption of 25 audio tokens per second and 175 text tokens per minute, blending to about $0.005 per minute), which this schema has no field for. Free tier is free of charge. No context window or max output token count is published for this endpoint, so both fields are null rather than inherited from a sibling; the stated limit is duration — up to 1 hour of audio per request, dropping to 30 minutes when diarization or word-level timestamps are enabled. Caching, code execution, file search, function calling, image generation and thinking are all listed Not supported, as are the batch, flex and priority consumption options. Released August 2026 per Google's deprecations table — month only, which is all Google states, so the field carries 2026-08 rather than a guessed day — and that table says 'No shutdown date announced' with the row not gray. Added 2026-09-01: missing from the catalog since launch, one of four Google models invisible to the check-google-prices.mjs completeness column because all of its price cells are multi-rate (LEARNINGS #105).

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live
models.notes: Low-latency real-time speech-to-text over WebSockets: the Live API endpoint of Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, for bidirectional streaming audio transcription. Status ga because Google's models index badges the single Gemini 3.5 Transcribe card 'New Stable' and that card names both endpoints, gemini-3.5-transcribe and gemini-3.5-transcribe-live; read 2026-09-01. Paid-tier rates per 1M tokens: input $3.50 on audio, output $21.00 on text — both above the unary endpoint, which the sibling row carries. Google also publishes duration-equivalent figures for the same rates (roughly $0.005 per minute of audio in and $0.004 per minute of text out, on an assumption of 25 audio tokens per second and 175 text tokens per minute, blending to about $0.009 per minute for Live Transcribe), a unit this schema has no field for. Free tier is free of charge. Grounding with Google Search is Not Supported. Feature parity with the unary endpoint is partial and Google states the differences: language auto-detection and custom vocabulary biasing yes, but word-level timestamps and speaker diarization NOT supported, and sessions are capped at 10 minutes rather than the 1 hour the file endpoint allows. No context window or max output token count is published, so both fields are null. Released August 2026 per Google's deprecations table — month only, which is all Google states — with 'No shutdown date announced' and the row not gray. Added 2026-09-01 alongside gemini-3.5-transcribe (LEARNINGS #105).

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
models.notes: Text-to-speech model: text in, audio out. GA per Google's September 22, 2026 release note, headed 'Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS generally available (GA)', which calls it the 'flagship creative TTS model engineered for studio-grade voice fidelity, nuanced acting, regional dialects, and long-form multi-turn stability'. THE PRICE FIELDS CARRY THE COLUMN IN FORCE THROUGH 2026-12-31, not the 2027 one: Google prices this model on a two-date schedule. Paid-tier Standard per 1M tokens is $0.50 input (text) / $9.00 output (audio) / $0.125 context caching through December 31, 2026, doubling to $1.00 / $18.00 / $0.25 starting January 1, 2027. Other tiers on the same two dates: Batch $0.25 / $4.50 (caching $0.0625) then $0.50 / $9.00 (caching $0.125); Flex $0.25 / $4.50 (caching $0.025) then $0.50 / $9.00 (caching $0.05); Priority $0.90 / $16.20 (caching $0.225) then $1.80 / $32.40 (caching $0.45). Cache storage, which this schema has no field for, is $0.50 per 1M tokens per hour through 2026-12-31 and $1.00 from 2027-01-01. Free tier is 'Free of charge' on Standard and Priority and 'Not available' on Batch and Flex. Audio tokens are billed at 25 tokens per second of audio. The model page gives an 8,192-token input limit and a 16,384-token output limit, text in and audio out, 130 input languages auto-detected, caching supported, and no thinking, function calling, grounding or Live API; Batch, Flex and Priority are all supported. Default output is WAV with a RIFF header, a change from earlier Gemini TTS models that returned raw PCM. Released 2026-09-22 per both the release note and the deprecations table ('No shutdown date announced', row not gray); the model page's 'Latest update' field says July 2026, which is coarser and older, so it is not used. Google publishes no knowledge cutoff. Google's deprecations table names this model, first, as the replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview. Added 2026-09-24, two days after launch.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS
models.notes: Text-to-speech model: text in, audio out. Input $1.00 (text), output $20.00 (audio); batch $0.50 / $10.00. Audio tokens are billed at 25 tokens per second of audio. Until 2026-10-06 Google stated "No shutdown date announced" and the status was held at preview. On the 2026-10-07 read Google's deprecations table published a shutdown date of November 17, 2026 for this endpoint (row not grey, so it was still running), so status became deprecated. Google later MOVED that date: the 2026-11-16 read of the deprecations table (aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md) gives December 18, 2026, with the row still outside the "Deprecated models" section, i.e. still running. retires_on carries December 18, 2026; Google does not date the edit, and it happened between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-16 (the reader was blind in that window). Google publishes shutdown dates as "the earliest possible dates on which a model might be retired". Until 2026-09-22 Google named no replacement; that day's deprecations table added 'gemini-3.8-flash-tts or gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts'. The replacement field holds one id and carries the first-named, gemini-3.8-flash-tts, in the table's own order - but both are first-party migration targets, and the same day's release note describes gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts as 'built to replace gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview'. Both successors are cheaper than this model on the rates in force through 2026-12-31 (output $9.00 and $6.00 against $20.00). Released February 26, 2026, the date in the Release date column of Google's deprecations table. Until 2026-09-24 that table listed this id in two rows, one dated February 26, 2026 carrying the replacement and one dated April 13, 2026 with none, and the released field held April 13; by the 2026-09-25 read Google had removed the April 13 row, leaving February 26 as the only date it publishes. Google's current models page publishes no input/output token limits for this endpoint (read 2026-08-19), so context_window and max_output_tokens are null rather than carried over from a page that no longer states them. Lifecycle read first-party from Google's deprecations table on 2026-08-19 and re-read 2026-09-25.
